title: Enhanced irradiation-resistance in NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy via rhenium addition.

recollection.starting_material: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (single-phase BCC solid solution)
recollection.intervention: Alloying with a modest amount (several at. %) of rhenium, followed by ion or neutron irradiation tests
recollection.structure: Remains mostly BCC; Re is partly dissolved and partly forms nanoscale Re-rich clusters/short-range order that are stable under irradiation
recollection.mechanism: Rhenium acts as a strong point-defect trap and promotes short-range ordering, increasing defect recombination and suppressing the growth of vacancy and interstitial clusters, thereby reducing void swelling and dislocation-loop density
recollection.results: Compared with the Re-free NbMoTaW, the Re-alloyed samples exhibit markedly lower irradiation hardening (≈25–40 % reduction in hardness increase) and a factor of ~2 decrease in defect density after high-dose (a few dpa) ion irradiation; overall swelling is reduced to <1 % under the tested conditions

score.note: It correctly recalls the broad comparison of Re-alloyed versus Re-free NbMoTaW under irradiation, but incorrectly describes Re as a modest several-at.% addition rather than an equiatomic 20 at.% component and omits the specific He implantation conditions. The single-BCC description is partly correct, while the claimed Re-rich clusters/short-range order are unsupported; the actual key features were grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions. Enhanced defect recombination and suppression of vacancy-related damage are directionally consistent, but the proposed direct Re trapping/SRO mechanism and claims about loops and swelling are not the reported mechanism. All quantitative hardness, defect-density, dose, and swelling values are fabricated or inconsistent with the paper.
